pluja-explicacio: Precipitation is all the water that falls from the sky: rain, drizzle, snow or hail. For each hour you can see the weather, how many millimeters are expected and the chance of rain.
pluja-idea: one millimeter is one liter of water per square meter. Less than 1 mm in an hour is drizzle; 2 to 5 mm is moderate rain that really gets you wet; more than 10 mm is a heavy downpour.
vent-desc-1: light wind, you feel it on your face
vent-desc-2: moderate wind, it sways branches and raises dust
vent-desc-3: strong wind, hard to walk against
vent-velocitat: it's the ten-minute average, measured ten meters above the ground. The arrow on the chart points where the wind is going, and the letters say where it comes from: a NW wind blows from the northwest.
vent-ratxes-explicacio: short bursts of wind, lasting a few seconds, that can be much stronger than the average. If you're cycling, riding a motorbike or sailing, look at the gusts first.
sol-alba-explicacio: it starts to get light even though the sun hasn't risen yet. That's when the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon (civil twilight).
sol-sortida-explicacio: the sun peeks over the horizon.
sol-posta-explicacio: the sun disappears completely below the horizon.
sol-capvespre-explicacio: the last light of the day; after this, it's dark.
uv-explicacio: The UV index tells you how strongly the sun burns. It goes from 0 to 11 or more: the higher it is, the less time it takes for your skin to burn and the more you need to protect your eyes.
uv-0-consell: You can be outside without worrying much. If you have very fair skin, sunglasses won't hurt.
uv-1-consell: Around midday, look for shade and wear sunscreen, a cap and sunglasses if you'll be in the sun for a while.
uv-2-consell: Real protection: SPF 30 or higher sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and clothes that cover you. Avoid the sun from noon to 4 p.m.
uv-3-titol: 8 or more, very high to extreme.
uv-3-consell: Your skin can burn in a few minutes. If your shadow is shorter than you are, the sun is strong: stay in the shade and protect yourself well.
aire-consell-2: Fine for most people. If you have asthma or heart problems, you may notice it during intense exercise.
aire-consell-3: Better to avoid intense exercise outdoors, especially if you're sensitive to pollution.
aire-consell-4: Avoid physical activity outdoors and, if you can, stay inside.
aire-explicacio: ICA is the official scale of the Spanish Ministry for the Ecological Transition, the same one the Government of Catalonia uses. It looks at five pollutants, and the overall rating is that of the worst one.
aire-calcul: particles (PM2.5 and PM10) as the average of the last 24 hours, ozone over the last 8 hours, and nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide over the last hour. In cities, nitrogen dioxide comes mostly from traffic.
aire-font: the European Copernicus model (CAMS), not a specific station, so the values may differ a little from the official measurements in your neighborhood.
visibilitat-explicacio: Visibility is how far away you can make out a large object, like a mountain or a building. Fog, rain, dust, smoke or haze reduce it.
visibilitat-escala: more than 20 km, excellent (days when you can see mountains far away); 10 to 20 km, good; 4 to 10 km, moderate; 1 to 4 km, poor; less than 1 km, fog.
humitat-mitjana: Average for the rest of the day
rosada-desc-0: the air is dry and pleasant
humitat-relativa: how much water vapor the air holds compared with the most it could hold at that temperature. At 100%, the air can't take any more and fog or dew forms.
rosada-perque-titol: Why look at the dew point:
rosada-perque: it's the temperature the air would have to cool down to for the humidity to reach 100%. It tells you better than humidity whether it will feel muggy: the higher it is, the stickier.
pressio-explicacio: It's the weight of all the air above us. To compare places at different altitudes, it's given adjusted to sea level.
pressio-significat: above 1,020 hPa there's usually a high-pressure system and settled weather; below 1,005, low-pressure systems and unsettled weather. The trend matters more than the value: if it drops quickly, a change in the weather is on its way.
pressio-cos: some people say they notice sudden changes in pressure as headaches or aching joints.
quanta-descripcio: Your town's weather on the Windows taskbar, in English, with no news and no ads. “Quina barra!” is Catalan for “what nerve!”, and it has the nerve to sit right where the Hasefroch one used to be.
quanta-autor: Made by $1 with the help of Claude, Anthropic's AI.
actualitzacio-nota: It checks for a new version once a day. It never downloads or installs anything on its own: it lets you know and opens the GitHub page of the new version.
font-open-meteo: Forecast, air quality and sea: $1 (CC BY 4.0), with models from Météo-France, DWD (ICON), ECMWF and Copernicus (CAMS).
font-platges-enllac: open data from the Government of Catalonia
quanta-privadesa-text: It doesn't collect any of your data or use your connection to guess where you are: you choose the places. It only sends the coordinates of your saved places to the weather services to get the forecast. Your settings are saved only on your computer.
quanta-llicencia-text: Open source under the MIT license. You can use, copy, modify and share it freely, as long as you keep the copyright notice. It's provided as is, without any warranty.
mar-ara: waves from the $1, $2 m high, every $3 seconds, and a swell from the $4, $5 m high, every $6 seconds.
mar-alcada: this is the significant wave height: the average of the highest third of the waves. Every now and then a bigger one comes in.
mar-periode: the seconds between one wave and the next. The longer it is, the more power the wave carries and the more orderly it reaches the beach.
mar-fons-explicacio: waves that formed far away, with wind from somewhere else, and travel all the way to the coast. For surfing, it's what matters most: a swell of more than half a meter with a period of 8 seconds or more usually brings good waves, especially if the wind blows from the land out to sea.
mar-estat: it follows the Douglas scale, the same one Meteocat uses: rippled (up to 0.1 m), smooth (up to 0.5 m), slight (up to 1.25 m), moderate (up to 2.5 m), rough (up to 4 m) and, above that, very rough.
mar-font: Open-Meteo's wave model, for the point at sea closest to the place. It doesn't replace the warnings of the maritime rescue service or Meteocat.
platges-avui: Today's status, as reported by the beach services.
platges-fora-temporada: Out of season: this is the last reported status, from $1. The bathing season runs from June to September.
platges-banderes: green, swimming allowed; yellow, swim with caution; red, no swimming. The reason (swell, jellyfish, pollution...) appears in parentheses when it's reported.
platges-font: the Government of Catalonia's open data on beach status, updated every day of the season. The health quality of the water (tests by the Catalan Water Agency) can be checked on the PlatgesCat website.
